props.title: Fascination
props.initialSlug: Erotic vampire tale of seduction and blood ritual

sections.content: Jean Rollin's Fascination (1979) stands as a pivotal work in European erotic horror, blending vampiric themes with surrealist imagery. The film's hypnotic atmosphere draws from the French Gothic tradition while subverting expectations through its unique focus on an all-female cult of aristocratic blood-drinkers. Like Rollin's earlier Lips of Blood (1975) and The Shiver of the Vampires (1971), it eschews traditional vampire mythology for a more sensual, dreamlike approach that influenced later art-house horror like The Hunger (1983) and Claire Denis' Trouble Every Day (2001).

movies.title: Vampyros Lesbos
movies.slug: Jesús Franco's psychedelic vampire tale mixing exploitation with arthouse sensibilities

sections.content: The film's setting in 1905 France creates a decadent backdrop that echoes similar period-set erotic horror films like The Beast (1975) and Harry Kümel's Daughters of Darkness (1971). The use of the abandoned slaughterhouse location becomes both metaphorically rich and visually striking, predating similar industrial-Gothic settings in later films like Hellraiser (1987) and Interview with the Vampire (1994). Rollin's signature dreamlike pacing and emphasis on ritual and ceremony would later influence directors like Anna Biller, particularly in The Love Witch (2016).

The iconic scythe-wielding sequence with Brigitte Lahaie established a visual motif that resonated through horror cinema, appearing in various forms in films like The Company of Wolves (1984) and American Horror Story: Coven (2013). Rollin's blend of eroticism and death became a template for European horror directors, particularly visible in the works of Jean-Pierre Jeunet and Marc Caro's Delicatessen (1991) and Dario Argento's Inferno (1980). sections.content: Rollin's unique vision in Fascination helped establish a distinctly French approach to horror that emphasized atmosphere over shock, influencing contemporary films like Raw (2016) and Revenge (2017). The film's focus on female-centric horror narratives and its blending of sexuality with violence created a template for later works like Let the Right One In (2008) and A Girl Walks Home Alone at Night (2014).
